title.value: Break development work into phases for Copilot

introduction.value: The poster splits work into phases with explicit tasks so Copilot's agent works through development steps instead of everything at once.

method.value: The poster breaks a feature into explicit phases in a quick note, such as building the API, wiring middleware, and adding rate limits. For each phase they run a planning task in parallel with Traycer to get file-level changes, review and edit that plan line by line, then hand the approved plan to Copilot using Sonnet 4 to write the code instead of letting it decide architecture end to end.

outcome.value: They say this gets about 90% of the work done and produces clean code most of the time, while making review easier and limiting random codebase changes. The stated downside is that blind end-to-end agent runs waste time with wrong designs, and the planning step is less useful for very small tasks.

notes.value: Their main concrete catch is cost: they cite Copilot with Sonnet 4 at about $10 for roughly 300 requests.

source_text.body:
Break development work into phases for Copilot
The poster splits work into phases with explicit tasks so Copilot's agent works through development steps instead of everything at once.
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
The poster breaks a feature into explicit phases in a quick note, such as building the API, wiring middleware, and adding rate limits. For each phase they run a planning task in parallel with Traycer to get file-level changes, review and edit that plan line by line, then hand the approved plan to Copilot using Sonnet 4 to write the code instead of letting it decide architecture end to end.
How it went
They say this gets about 90% of the work done and produces clean code most of the time, while making review easier and limiting random codebase changes. The stated downside is that blind end-to-end agent runs waste time with wrong designs, and the planning step is less useful for very small tasks.
Worth knowing
Their main concrete catch is cost: they cite Copilot with Sonnet 4 at about $10 for roughly 300 requests.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
I'm building [project description]. Break the work into [number] phases with explicit tasks in each, and show me the plan first. Then do only Phase 1, stop, and summarize what you did so I can review it before we start the next phase.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1lwg11b/youre_probably_using_copilot_the_wrong_way
